title: 1. Audit transient hits versus sustained axial-roll success
hypothesis: Transient axial-spin bursts inflate any-hit episode success because a pen can briefly satisfy the native predicate before losing stable in-hand rotation.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is any native-success step in an episode; the alternative requires native success throughout the final 60 steps, with early termination counted as failure. A 20-percentage-point reduction on identical trajectories would materially change expert qualification.

protocol.command: gpu run 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --research-protocol episode_rule_audit'
code_changes: Extend the existing smoke script and config with the declared research-protocol CLI and profile; freeze ten probe cases per stage before rollout.

Add an Isaac manifest/schema adapter under lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin: record reset provenance, named 157-d observation fields, normalized-to-environment action mapping, termination, and all 360 step predicates.
Evaluate fixed neutral-pose and open-loop digit-oscillation controllers on each case; score both episode reducers offline from the same traces, pooling stages with equal weight.
Add reducer and quaternion-axis tests that distinguish long-axis roll from end-over-end rotation; retain per-stage results and raw angular velocity.
Document the sustained rule as the preregistered qualification rule for the following studies, not as an already validated task definition; do not promote a policy in this audit.

falsified_by: A paired interval entirely above a sustained-minus-any-hit difference of -0.20 rules out the predicted reduction on these diagnostic controllers; an interval containing zero is inconclusive about a directional difference.

controls.baseline: any_hit reducer on identical trajectories (same 60 episodes, offline)
controls.controllers: neutral_pose (default joint targets) and open_loop_digit_oscillation (amp 0.35, 1.5 Hz, staggered phases), frozen in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/controllers.py before the probe cases ran
controls.reproducibility: one rollout per process; a first rollout is bit-identical across fresh processes (debug seed 4099), a second rollout in the same process is not

notes: Prediction (sustained lowers success by >= 0.20 vs any-hit) holds: -0.983, t interval [-1.017, -0.950], n=60 pooled with equal weight per stage (20 episodes each).

Any-hit is degenerate: the neutral hand that holds nothing scores 1.0/1.0/0.9 per stage, its first hit at steps 5-8 as the dropped pen lands and rolls (max |spin| up to 75 rad/s), and it drops the pen in 29/30 episodes (completed 0.0/0.0/0.1).

The open-loop oscillator keeps the pen in hand to time-out in 10/10, 10/10 and 9/10 episodes and satisfies the per-step predicate on 84%/56%/39% of the final 60 steps (stage 1/2/3) with mean |roll| about 4 rad/s, but never on all 60, so sustained success is 0 everywhere. A rolling pen driven by a sinusoid passes through low spin twice per cycle; whether 'all 60 steps' is too strict for a periodic gait is an open design question for R-039 (a tail-fraction rule would score this oscillator very differently).
Transverse (end-over-end) angular speed stays small (0.36-0.72 rad/s mean under the oscillator): the task measures and rewards roll about the long axis only.

Excursions from protocol.code_changes: the smoke script gained --research-protocol/--build-manifests/--stage/--controller; a runner bug (previous run's action leaking into last_action) and in-process non-reproducibility were found and fixed before the probe run; both on debug seed 4099.

verdicts.reasoning: The named any-hit baseline was measured on identical trajectories: success fell from 0.9833 to 0.0000 under sustained scoring across 60 episodes [logs/pen_spin/r038_episode_rule_audit/summary.json]. The paired sustained-minus-any-hit difference was -0.9833, with reported 95% interval [-1.0167, -0.9500], entirely below the predicted -0.20 threshold [logs/pen_spin/r038_episode_rule_audit/summary.json]. Although the interval extends below the feasible difference bound, its upper endpoint strongly supports the preregistered reduction [logs/pen_spin/r038_episode_rule_audit/summary.json]. This establishes sensitivity to the episode reducer on these diagnostic controllers, not that the sustained rule is a validated definition of expert-quality rotation [logs/pen_spin/r038_episode_rule_audit/summary.json].

On the identical 60 trajectories, sustained success is 0.000 against any-hit 0.983: paired difference -0.983, t interval [-1.017, -0.950], far beyond the predicted 0.20 drop. The mechanism is visible directly: a neutral hand that holds nothing scores any-hit 1.0/1.0/0.9 per stage, with first hits at steps 5-8 as the dropped pen lands and rolls, while dropping the pen in 29/30 episodes. Any-hit cannot serve as the qualification rule. Caveat agreed in triage: this validates that any-hit is degenerate, not that 'all of the final 60 steps' is the right rule. The open-loop oscillator holds the pen to time-out in 29/30 episodes with 84/56/39% of tail steps passing, yet scores 0 under sustained because a sinusoidal gait dips below threshold twice per cycle. (Recorded after the advisor's analyse call because my first verdict call failed on a non-numeric confidence; the reasoning was written before reading it.)
verdicts.next_experiment: Re-triage R-039 (scripted feedback gait) with the sustained rule frozen as the qualification reducer, and report tail-hit fraction beside it so a periodic gait's near-misses are visible. Open question to propose: is 'all 60 steps' too strict for any periodic gait, i.e. should the rule be a tail-fraction or mean-rate criterion? Decide it before any expert is qualified, not after.

direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: This establishes a reproducible Isaac evaluation path and measures how much episode qualification changes when transient hits no longer suffice. Reusing identical trajectories for both reducers gives high information value for 60 simulator episodes and zero LLM calls. Its weakest point is that neutral and open-loop controllers may produce few native-success hits, limiting conclusions about eventual experts; the sustained rule remains provisional, not validated by this comparison.

implementer.reasoning: Every later pen-spin idea needs three things this builds: a manifest-driven Isaac rollout with case-determined resets (Isaac's batched reset draws from the global torch RNG, so the adapter must write each case's pen pose itself rather than reseed), a named 157-d observation schema, and a declared episode success rule. The env only defines per-step success. A free-falling or settling pen can roll faster than 1 rad/s within 0.10 m for a few steps after reset, so any-hit may score a neutral hand as successful. That makes the audit informative even with trivial controllers, at 60 episodes and no calls. Agreed limit: the sustained rule is preregistered, not validated.
